```{=html}
Chains onto elev_z_flux.csv (elevation_and_z_star.qmd's output), same
"join before tier" position as veg and (eventually) slope. Computes
mean wind speed (and max gust) over each sediment trap's actual
deployment window -- Date.placed.in.field to Date.removed.from.field
-- not a calendar-month average. Writes elev_z_wind_flux.csv.

SITE -> STATION MAPPING (as given, not yet corrected):
  CorteMadera, GiantMarsh, Buck'sLanding -> station 9414863
  SanPablo                                -> station 9415141
Known limitation, not fixed here: three sites currently share one
buoy's readings, which may not reflect real local wind conditions at
each of those three marshes individually. Flagged for later
correction, per your own note -- not addressed in this file.

COVERAGE GAP, REAL AND UNAVOIDABLE WITH CURRENT DATA: both station
files only cover 1/1/2025 through 7/13/2026. That covers the July
2025-June 2026 main campaign. It does NOT cover the July 2022-June
2023 repeat-year subset (2 marshes) -- those deployment windows will
get NA wind metrics, not a fabricated value. This also means USGS
flux data (entirely 2022-2023) cannot get wind metrics from this data
at all -- no usgs_wind.qmd built here for that reason; it would be
100% NA rows, not a useful file.

DUPLICATE COLUMN NAME IN THE RAW FILES: both CSVs have two columns
literally named "Direction" -- one numeric degrees (e.g. 113), one
compass abbreviation (e.g. "ESE"). R's read.csv() will auto-rename the
second to "Direction.1" by default; renamed explicitly below to
Direction_deg / Direction_compass so this isn't left to an implicit
default someone has to rediscover later.

MISSING READINGS: San Pablo's station has 44 missing Speed values
(gaps in the hourly record) -- handled with na.rm = TRUE in the
averaging, not imputed.
-->
```

```{r, load and clean both wind station files}
load_wind_station <- function(path, station_id) {
  raw <- read.csv(path, check.names = FALSE)
  # Explicit rename -- do not rely on read.csv's automatic ".1"
  # suffixing for the duplicate "Direction" columns; name by content
  # (first is numeric degrees, second is compass abbreviation),
  # confirmed by inspecting the raw column order directly.
  names(raw) <- c("datetime_raw", "wind_speed_kt", "direction_deg",
                   "direction_compass", "gust_kt", "x_flag", "r_flag")

  raw |>
    mutate(
      datetime = mdy_hm(datetime_raw),
      wind_speed_kt = as.numeric(wind_speed_kt),
      gust_kt = as.numeric(gust_kt),
      station_id = station_id
    ) |>
    select(station_id, datetime, wind_speed_kt, direction_deg, direction_compass, gust_kt)
}

)
```

```{r, compute mean wind speed over a deployment window}
# Not a calendar-month average -- averages every hourly reading whose
# timestamp falls within [deploy_start, deploy_end], inclusive. Returns
# n_obs alongside the mean so a window with very few matching readings
# (partial station coverage, or a short deployment) is visible rather
# than looking identical to a well-covered one.
# BOUNDARY ASSUMPTION, FLAGGED NOT RESOLVED: deploy_start/deploy_end
# are Date (calendar day), while station timestamps are full
# datetimes. R will coerce Date to midnight (00:00) for the
# comparison, so deploy_end effectively means "through the start of
# the removal day," not "through the end of it" -- readings from
# 1am-11pm on the actual removal day get excluded. Over a ~30-day
# window this is unlikely to move a mean much, but it's a real
# simplification, not something to assume away silently. If you want
# the full removal day included, change deploy_end below to
# `deploy_end + hours(23) + minutes(59)` (or similar) before comparing.
wind_metrics_for_window <- function(station_id, deploy_start, deploy_end) {
  station_df <- wind_by_station[[as.character(station_id)]]

  in_window <- station_df |>
    filter(datetime >= deploy_start, datetime <= deploy_end)

  tibble(
    mean_wind_speed_kt = mean(in_window$wind_speed_kt, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_gust_kt = max(in_window$gust_kt, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_obs = sum(!is.na(in_window$wind_speed_kt))
  )
}
```

```{r, load elevation-joined flux data, get distinct deployment windows}
elev_z_flux <- readr::read_csv("C:\\Users\\savan\\OneDrive - San Francisco State University\\ProjectData\\GitHub\\DepositionSFB\\data\\elev_z_flux.csv")

# Keyed on the ACTUAL placed/removed dates per Site, not assumed
# uniform across Tran/Dist/Replicate within a nominal collection round
# -- avoids redundant computation (many rows share a window) without
# assuming something about the field logistics that isn't confirmed.
deployment_windows <- elev_z_flux |>
  distinct(Site, Date.placed.in.field, Date.removed.from.field) |>
  left_join(site_station_map, by = "Site")

# Any Site with no station mapping at all would show up here as NA
# station_id -- confirms the crosswalk covers every Site actually
# present in the flux data before relying on it.
deployment_windows |> filter(is.na(station_id)) |> distinct(Site)
```

```{r, apply wind_metrics_for_window to every distinct deployment}
wind_by_window <- deployment_windows |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    wind_metrics_for_window(station_id, Date.placed.in.field, Date.removed.from.field)
  ) |>
  ungroup()

wind_by_window
```

```{r, join onto elev_z_flux and write}
elev_z_wind_flux <- elev_z_flux |>
  left_join(
    wind_by_window |> select(Site, Date.placed.in.field, Date.removed.from.field,
                              mean_wind_speed_kt, max_gust_kt, n_obs),
    by = c("Site", "Date.placed.in.field", "Date.removed.from.field")
  )

readr::write_csv(elev_z_wind_flux, "C:\\Users\\savan\\OneDrive - San Francisco State University\\ProjectData\\GitHub\\DepositionSFB\\data\\elev_z_wind_flux.csv")

nrow(elev_z_wind_flux) == nrow(elev_z_flux)   # confirms the join didn't fan out or drop rows
```

```{r}

# ============================================================
# WIND ROSE FUNCTION
# Takes a dataframe with a speed column and a direction column,
# groups readings into compass sectors + speed bands, and plots
# a polar bar chart. Call this once per rose you want.
# ============================================================
plot_wind_rose <- function(df,
                           speed_col = wind_speed_kt,   # column holding speed values
                           dir_col = direction_deg,     # column holding direction in degrees (0-360)
                           facet_var = NULL,             # optional: column to split into a grid (e.g. month)
                           speed_breaks = c(0, 5, 10, 15, 20, Inf),  # edges of the speed bins
                           speed_labels = c("0-5", "5-10", "10-15", "15-20", "20+"),  # labels for those bins
                           dir_bins = 16,                 # number of compass sectors (16 = standard 22.5° wedges)
                           title = "Wind Rose") {
  
  # --- tidy evaluation setup ---
  # enquo() lets you pass a bare column name (like wind_speed_kt, not "wind_speed_kt")
  # as a function argument, the same way you'd type it inside mutate() or filter().
  # The !! later "unquotes" it so R knows to actually use that column.
  speed_col <- enquo(speed_col)
  dir_col   <- enquo(dir_col)
  facet_var <- enquo(facet_var)
  has_facet <- !rlang::quo_is_null(facet_var)  # TRUE only if you actually passed a facet_var
  
  dir_width <- 360 / dir_bins  # width of each compass wedge in degrees (360/16 = 22.5)
  
  # --- clean and bin the data ---
  df_clean <- df |>
    filter(!is.na(!!speed_col), !is.na(!!dir_col)) |>  # drop rows missing speed or direction
    mutate(
      # cut() sorts each speed value into one of the bins defined above
      speed_bin = cut(!!speed_col, breaks = speed_breaks, labels = speed_labels,
                      right = FALSE, include.lowest = TRUE),
      # snaps each exact direction (e.g. 113°) to the nearest compass
      # sector center (e.g. 112.5° = ESE), then wraps anything past
      # 360 back around to 0 with %%
      dir_bin = (round(!!dir_col / dir_width) * dir_width) %% 360
    )
  
  # build the list of columns to group by -- always direction + speed bin,
  # plus the facet column too if one was given
  group_cols <- c("dir_bin", "speed_bin")
  if (has_facet) group_cols <- c(rlang::as_name(facet_var), group_cols)
  
  # --- count readings in each bin and convert to a percentage ---
  df_binned <- df_clean |>
    count(across(all_of(group_cols))) |>  # tally how many readings fall in each dir/speed combo
    group_by(across(all_of(if (has_facet) rlang::as_name(facet_var) else character(0)))) |>
    mutate(pct = n / sum(n) * 100) |>  # convert raw counts to % (so each rose/facet sums to 100%)
    ungroup()
  
  # --- build the plot ---
  p <- ggplot(df_binned, aes(x = dir_bin, y = pct, fill = speed_bin)) +
    geom_col(width = dir_width * 0.95, color = "white", linewidth = 0.1) +  # the wedges themselves
    coord_polar(start = -dir_width / 2 * pi / 180) +  # THIS is what bends the bars into a circle
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 315, 45),
                       labels = c("N", "NE", "E", "SE", "S", "SW", "W", "NW"),  # compass labels
                       limits = c(-dir_width / 2, 360 - dir_width / 2)) +
    scale_fill_viridis_d(name = "Speed (kt)") +  # colorblind-friendly palette for the speed bins
    # str_wrap keeps long titles from running off the edge of the image;
    # a plain "-" (not an en dash –) avoids a font rendering issue
    labs(title = stringr::str_wrap(title, width = 45), x = NULL, y = "Frequency (%)") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
          plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10))
  
  # if a facet_var was given, split into a small-multiples grid (one rose per group)
  if (has_facet) {
    p <- p + facet_wrap(vars(!!facet_var), ncol = 4) +
      theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 6))  # shrink labels since panels are smaller
  }
  p
}
```

```{r}

# ---- STATION 9415141: one rose per month, restricted to the main
# campaign window (July 2025 - June 2026) ----
#
# CHANGED FROM BEFORE: previously this pooled every year present in
# the data for a given calendar month (e.g. all Januaries, whether
# 2025 or 2026, combined). Now it's filtered to a single 12-month
# span first, so each month panel reflects ONE occurrence of that
# month, not a pooled average across years.
#
# Also reordered the facets to run Jul -> Jun (matching the campaign
# window chronologically) instead of R's default Jan -> Dec calendar
# order -- done by turning month_label into a factor with explicit
# levels in that order.

wind_9415141_monthly <- wind_9415141 |>
  # keep only readings inside the July 2025-June 2026 campaign window
  filter(datetime >= as.POSIXct("2025-07-01 00:00:00"),
         datetime <= as.POSIXct("2026-06-30 23:59:59")) |>
  mutate(
    month_label = month(datetime, label = TRUE, abbr = TRUE),
    # reorder so facets display Jul first, Jun last (not alphabetical/calendar order)
    month_label = factor(month_label, levels = c("Jul","Aug","Sep","Oct","Nov","Dec",
                                                 "Jan","Feb","Mar","Apr","May","Jun"))
  )

rose_9415141_monthly <- plot_wind_rose(
  wind_9415141_monthly,
  facet_var = month_label,
  title = "Wind Rose by Month (Jul 2025-Jun 2026) - Station 9415141 (San Pablo)"
)
rose_9415141_monthly  # prints the plot in the Quarto output

ggsave(
  "C:\\Users\\savan\\OneDrive - San Francisco State University\\ProjectData\\GitHub\\DepositionSFB\\figures\\windrose_9415141_by_month.png",
  rose_9415141_monthly, width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 300
)

```

```{r}

# ---- MAY-JUL 2026: one combined rose per station (no facet) ----
# Unlike the monthly roses above, this filters to a SPECIFIC year
# (2026) rather than pooling all years together, and doesn't split
# into month-by-month panels -- one rose per station for the whole
# window.
#
# NOTE: station data only goes through 2026-07-13, so "July" here
# is a partial month (13 of 31 days). Also, this is NOT called
# "May-Aug" because August 2026 doesn't exist in the data at all yet.

wind_9414863_mayjul26 <- wind_9414863 |>
  filter(year(datetime) == 2026, month(datetime) %in% 5:7)  # keep only May, Jun, Jul of 2026
wind_9415141_mayjul26 <- wind_9415141 |>
  filter(year(datetime) == 2026, month(datetime) %in% 5:7)

nrow(wind_9414863_mayjul26)
range(wind_9414863_mayjul26$datetime)
```
